name: Might and Magic
description: Questions covering: Might and Magic I, Might and Magic II, Might and Magic III...

questions.question: In Might and Magic I, what is the name of the town where the adventure begins?
questions.explanation_correct: Sorpigal is the starting town in Might and Magic I. It is where the player first begins exploration and quests.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are locations from later games or other settings in the series. They are not the initial town in Might and Magic I.

questions.question: In Might and Magic II, which character serves as the central antagonist?
questions.explanation_correct: Sheltem is the principal antagonist in Might and Magic II. He is a recurring figure tied to the series' early plotlines.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names belong to different roles or different games in the franchise. They are not the main opponent in Might and Magic II.

questions.question: What is the setting named in the subtitle of Might and Magic III?
questions.explanation_correct: The third main RPG is titled Might and Magic III: Isles of Terra; its story takes place on the Isles of Terra.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names refer to places associated with later games.

questions.question: Which earlier Might and Magic game is subtitled Gates to Another World?
questions.explanation_correct: Might and Magic II: Gates to Another World takes place on CRON. The third game is Isles of Terra.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other numbered entries have different subtitles and settings.

questions.question: Under what name does Sheltem rule the Darkside in Might and Magic V?
questions.explanation_correct: In Darkside of Xeen, the antagonist called Alamar is revealed to be Sheltem.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Corak opposes Sheltem; the other characters are not the alias specified in the question.

questions.question: In Might and Magic VI, which continent is the game primarily set on?
questions.explanation_correct: Enroth is the continent where Might and Magic VI takes place. It is the main setting for the game’s events.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are settings from different titles or related worlds. They are not the continent of Might and Magic VI.

questions.question: In Might and Magic VII, what is the name of the starting region?
questions.explanation_correct: Emerald Island is the starting region in Might and Magic VII. The game begins there before the broader world opens up.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are regions from other games or different locations in the franchise. They are not the starting region of Might and Magic VII.

questions.question: In Might and Magic VIII, what is the name of the main continent?
questions.explanation_correct: Jadame is the main continent in Might and Magic VIII. It serves as the central setting for that installment.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are continents or worlds from other entries in the series. They are not the main continent of Might and Magic VIII.

questions.question: In Might and Magic IX, what is the primary setting called?
questions.explanation_correct: Chedian is the primary setting for Might and Magic IX. It is the area in which the game’s events are centered.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are locations from different games or worlds in the franchise. They are not the primary setting of Might and Magic IX.

questions.subcategory: Heroes of Might and Magic III
questions.question: Which Heroes III Necropolis hero specializes in the Sorcery secondary skill?
questions.explanation_correct: Sandro is a Necropolis Necromancer whose specialty improves Sorcery.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Isra and Vidomina specialize in Necromancy, while Vokial specializes in Vampires.

questions.subcategory: Heroes of Might and Magic III
questions.question: Which Heroes of Might and Magic III hero belongs to the Inferno faction?
questions.explanation_correct: Xyron is an Inferno Heretic hero; the question does not identify him as the unique ruler of all Inferno towns.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Vidomina, Orrin and Kyrre are associated with other hero classes and towns.

questions.subcategory: Heroes of Might and Magic IV
questions.question: Who is the protagonist of the Haven/Life campaign The True Blade in Heroes of Might and Magic IV?
questions.explanation_correct: The True Blade follows Lysander. Gauldoth is the protagonist of the Necropolis/Death campaign Half-Dead.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Elwin is associated with the Nature campaign and Tawni with the Chaos campaign.

questions.subcategory: Heroes of Might and Magic V
questions.question: Which Heroes of Might and Magic V ruler is married to Isabel at the beginning of the campaign?
questions.explanation_correct: Nicolai Griffin is the ruler of the Griffin Empire and Isabel’s husband in the Heroes V story.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Wulfstan and Raelag appear in other roles, while Gavin Magnus belongs to another continuity.

questions.question: Who is credited as the original creator of the Might and Magic franchise?
questions.explanation_correct: Jon Van Caneghem created the Might and Magic franchise. He was the designer behind the original series.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are notable game industry figures, but they did not originate the Might and Magic franchise.

questions.question: What is the name of the popular turn-based strategy sub-series that began in 1995 within the Might and Magic universe?
questions.explanation_correct: Heroes of Might and Magic is the acclaimed spin-off series focusing on army management and city building.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Age of Wonders and Disciples are rival fantasy strategy series, while Master of Orion is sci-fi.

questions.question: Which dynasty includes the brothers Roland and Archibald in Heroes of Might and Magic II?
questions.explanation_correct: Roland and Archibald belong to the Ironfist dynasty; their succession conflict is central to Heroes II.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are not the surname of the brothers in that story.

questions.question: In the journal included with Might and Magic III, whom is Corak searching for?
questions.explanation_correct: Corak describes his search for his nemesis Sheltem in the Might and Magic III manual.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other characters are not the adversary named in Corak’s journal.

questions.question: Which insectoid race appears in Might and Magic lore?
questions.explanation_correct: The Kreegans are alien invaders portrayed with demonic and insect-like traits in the Enroth-era setting.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Naga, dwarves and elves are different fantasy peoples or creatures; the details vary across games and continuities.

questions.question: What are the ancient, technologically advanced beings in the original Might and Magic continuity called?
questions.explanation_correct: The Ancients are an advanced civilization associated with the creation and seeding of worlds in the original continuity.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other labels are not the specific name requested; later games use different continuities.

questions.question: Which type of vehicle is used by the party to travel from the Dagger Wound Islands to the mainland in Might and Magic VIII?
questions.explanation_correct: The party begins on the Dagger Wound Islands and can travel by ship to Ravenshore on the mainland.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The listed train, airship and car are not the regular initial route from the islands to Ravenshore.

questions.question: In Might and Magic VII, Archibald Ironfist leads a guild of necromancers associated with which land?
questions.explanation_correct: Archibald is associated with the Necromancers’ Guild in Deyja during Might and Magic VII; his role changes during the story.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AvLee, Bracada and Erathia are other regions of Antagarich.

questions.question: Which Ironfist brother is king of Enroth during the events of Might and Magic VI?
questions.explanation_correct: Roland Ironfist is the king of Enroth at the start of the events surrounding Might and Magic VI.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Archibald is Roland’s brother and rival; kingship varies across the series timeline.

questions.question: Who was the usurping brother of Roland?
questions.explanation_correct: Archibald Ironfist is Roland's brother and the one who usurps power in the storyline. He is a major antagonist in the series.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are either Roland himself or unrelated characters, not the brother who seized power.

questions.question: Which faction is the Inferno-associated demonic group in Might and Magic?
questions.explanation_correct: Kreegans are the demonic faction associated with Inferno in Might and Magic. They are portrayed as fiendish invaders and servants of chaos.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different factions or town alignments, not the demonic group tied to Inferno.

questions.question: Which elven kingdom is located in Antagarich?
questions.explanation_correct: AvLee is the elven kingdom in Antagarich. It is one of the major regions in the Heroes of Might and Magic III setting.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different nations in Antagarich, but they are not the elven kingdom.

questions.question: Which nation in Antagarich is ruled by necromancers?
questions.explanation_correct: Deyja is the necromancer nation in Antagarich. It is associated with death magic and undead forces.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are separate nations or kingdoms, not the necromancer domain.

questions.question: Which wizard nation is located in Antagarich?
questions.explanation_correct: Bracada is the wizard nation in Antagarich. It is known as the domain of mages and arcane learning.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are other nations in the setting, but they are not the wizard realm.

questions.question: What is the title artifact sought during the Heroes III expansion Armageddon’s Blade?
questions.explanation_correct: Armageddon’s Blade is the namesake artifact of the Heroes III expansion; the campaign involves several characters and factions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are not the title artifact named by the expansion.

questions.question: Which playable class is traditionally associated with a blend of magic and nature in Might and Magic?
questions.explanation_correct: The Druid class focuses on nature magic and spellcasting. It blends elemental and supportive magic in the series.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Clerics and sorcerers are spellcasters too; the question asks about the nature-associated Druid class.

questions.question: Which undead creature in Heroes III upgrades to a Power Lich?
questions.explanation_correct: The Lich upgrades to a Power Lich in the Necropolis creature lineup.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other undead creatures have their own separate upgrade paths.

questions.question: What is the subtitle of Might and Magic VI?
questions.explanation_correct: Might and Magic VI is subtitled Mandate of Heaven. It is the sixth main entry in the RPG series.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are not subtitles of Might and Magic VI. They belong to unrelated works or are invented.

questions.question: What is the subtitle of Might and Magic VII?
questions.explanation_correct: Might and Magic VII is subtitled For Blood and Honor. This subtitle appears with the game's full title.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are not the subtitle of Might and Magic VII. They do not match the game's official title.

questions.question: What is the subtitle of Might and Magic VIII?
questions.explanation_correct: Might and Magic VIII is subtitled Day of the Destroyer. It is the eighth main game in the series.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are not the subtitle of Might and Magic VIII. They are not official subtitles from the series.

questions.question: Which numbered mainline Might and Magic RPG was released without an official subtitle in 2002?
questions.explanation_correct: The game was released as Might and Magic IX. “Writ of Fate” was a working title, not its official released subtitle.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other numbered entries carry the subtitles The Mandate of Heaven, For Blood and Honor, and Day of the Destroyer.

questions.question: Which Heroes III Inferno Heretic specializes in the Inferno spell?
questions.explanation_correct: Xyron specializes in the Inferno spell, not Fireball.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Zydar, Calh and Ash are other Inferno heroes with different specialties.

questions.question: Which Heroes III Necromancer-class hero specializes in the Necromancy skill?
questions.explanation_correct: Vidomina is a Necromancer with a Necromancy specialty; Isra is a Death Knight who also specializes in Necromancy.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sandro, Thant and Xsi have different specialties.

questions.question: Which Castle Cleric specializes in the Bless spell in Heroes III?
questions.explanation_correct: Adela specializes in Bless. Caitlin is a Cleric whose specialty provides extra gold.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Orrin specializes in Archery and Christian in Ballistics; Caitlin has a gold specialty.

questions.question: Which studio developed Heroes of Might and Magic II?
questions.explanation_correct: New World Computing developed Heroes of Might and Magic II.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other studios developed different games; Wizard and Warlock are separate town alignments in Heroes II.

questions.question: In Heroes III, what does a Necropolis Skeleton Transformer do to creatures placed in it?
options: Teaches a hero the Fly spell
questions.explanation_correct: The Skeleton Transformer converts creatures brought to it into skeletons, subject to game-specific conversion rules.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other actions are not the function of the Necropolis building.

questions.question: Who is the protagonist of the Necropolis campaign “Half-Dead” in Heroes of Might and Magic IV?
questions.explanation_correct: Gauldoth is the protagonist of the Death-aligned Necropolis campaign “Half-Dead.”
questions.explanation_incorrect: Elwin, Lysander, and Tawni are protagonists of other Heroes IV campaigns.

questions.question: Which creature is the upgraded form of the Green Dragon in the Heroes III Rampart lineup?
questions.explanation_correct: In Heroes III, the Rampart Green Dragon upgrades to the Gold Dragon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other dragons are separate creature types and upgrade lines.

questions.question: In Heroes III: The Shadow of Death, what does the Admiral’s Hat combination artifact help preserve when a hero boards or leaves a ship?
questions.explanation_correct: The Admiral’s Hat reduces the movement penalty when transitioning between land and a ship; it does not grant unlimited movement.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Its effect concerns travel rather than infinite movement or the other listed resources.

questions.question: In Heroes III, which school of magic includes the Resurrection spell?
questions.explanation_correct: Resurrection is an Earth Magic spell in Heroes III. Magic schools and healing spells differ between entries.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are also Heroes III magic schools, but Resurrection belongs to Earth Magic.

questions.question: Which Heroes III town is the undead faction?
questions.explanation_correct: Necropolis is the undead town in Heroes of Might and Magic III. It is centered on skeletons, vampires, and other undead units.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other towns belong to different factions and unit themes. They are not the undead town.

questions.question: What is the world where the Heroes IV campaigns take place?
questions.explanation_correct: Axeoth is the world where Heroes IV is set, rather than the name of a single continent.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Erathia and Antagarich refer to places in the earlier Enroth setting.

questions.question: What is the starting town in Might and Magic VI?
questions.explanation_correct: New Sorpigal is the starting location for Might and Magic VI. It is the first town players typically begin from.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are not the opening town of Might and Magic VI. They do not match the game’s starting location.

questions.question: What city is the capital of Erathia in Heroes of Might and Magic III?
questions.explanation_correct: Steadwick is the capital city of Erathia, the kingdom associated with Queen Catherine’s campaign.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Erathia is a kingdom, not the city name; the other places are different locations.

questions.question: Which land is associated with the Kreegan Inferno forces in Heroes III?
questions.explanation_correct: Eeofol is associated with the Kreegan Inferno forces; Nighon is associated with the underground Dungeon faction.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bracada and Tatalia correspond to other lands and factions.

questions.question: Which region is the Dungeon homeland in Heroes III?
questions.explanation_correct: Nighon is the homeland associated with the Dungeon faction in Heroes III. It is the subterranean realm linked to Dungeon forces.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are not the Dungeon homeland. They belong to different factions or are not used as the Dungeon origin.

questions.question: What is the main continent of Might and Magic VII?
questions.explanation_correct: Antagarich is the principal continent in Might and Magic VII. The game’s story unfolds across that major landmass.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other continents belong to different entries or settings in the series. They are not the main continent for Might and Magic VII.

questions.question: Which Heroes III Death Knight specializes in the Necromancy secondary skill?
questions.explanation_correct: Isra is a Death Knight specializing in Necromancy. Vidomina also has a Necromancy specialty, but is a Necromancer-class hero.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sandro specializes in Sorcery, Thant in Animate Dead and Galthran in Skeletons.

questions.question: Which Heroes III Ranger specializes in Logistics?
questions.explanation_correct: Kyrre is a Rampart Ranger with a Logistics specialty; Mephala is also a Ranger, with an Armorer specialty.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mephala is a Ranger too, but does not have Kyrre’s Logistics specialty; the others have different roles.

questions.question: What is the class of the recruitable companion Cauri Blackthorne in Might and Magic VIII?
questions.explanation_correct: Cauri Blackthorne is a Dark Elf Patriarch and can be recruited after being freed in Murmurwoods.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fredrick Talimere is a Cleric, while Devlin Arcanus is a recruitable Necromancer.

questions.question: What is the name of the original arbiter in Harmondale in Might and Magic VII?
questions.explanation_correct: Judge Grey initially arbitrates the Harmondale dispute; the player can later select a successor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are different characters or officials in the series.

questions.question: Which creature appears in the Wizard town lineup in Heroes of Might and Magic II?
questions.explanation_correct: The Wizard town in Heroes II can recruit Giants and their upgraded Titans.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other creatures are associated with the Necromancer, Sorceress or Warlock lineups.

questions.question: In Heroes III, which town is the Minotaur faction associated with?
questions.explanation_correct: Dungeon is the Heroes III town associated with Minotaurs. The other options are different faction towns in the same game.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Each option is a Heroes III town, but only one is tied to Minotaurs. The others belong to other factions.

questions.question: In Might and Magic VI, where is the Oracle located?
questions.explanation_correct: The Oracle is located in the city of Free Haven in Might and Magic VI.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are different locations in the same game.

questions.question: Which character is the protagonist of the Preserve/Nature campaign Elwin and Shaera in Heroes IV?
questions.explanation_correct: The Nature campaign follows Elwin and Shaera; Tawni’s campaign is associated with Chaos.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gauldoth and Lysander lead other Heroes IV campaigns.

questions.question: What building in Heroes III allows visiting heroes to learn available spells?
questions.explanation_correct: Heroes with a spell book can learn the town’s available spells by visiting a Mage Guild.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other buildings serve other town functions.

questions.question: Which queen returns to Erathia in the opening story of Heroes of Might and Magic III?
questions.explanation_correct: Queen Catherine returns to Erathia in the opening story after the death of her father, King Nicolas Gryphonheart.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are different characters in the franchise.

questions.question: Where does the player’s adventure begin in Might and Magic VIII?
questions.explanation_correct: The Might and Magic VIII manual describes the party’s initial task of leaving the Dagger Wound Islands for Jadame’s mainland.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ravenshore is reached later; the other options refer to different regions.

questions.question: In Heroes III, which Inferno hero is named among the faction’s roster?
questions.explanation_correct: Nymus is a female Demoniac hero associated with Inferno in Heroes III.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are not the Inferno hero identified in the question.

questions.question: In Heroes III, what item does a hero need in order to record and cast learned spells?
questions.explanation_correct: A hero needs a spell book to record spells and cast them; Mage Guilds can provide one for purchase.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A spyglass, shipyard and catapult serve different functions.

questions.question: Which character appears as a barbarian hero in multiple Might and Magic games, including Heroes III?
questions.explanation_correct: Crag Hack is a recurring barbarian hero associated with the franchise.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other characters are associated with different roles.

questions.question: In Might and Magic VII, which advisor represents the Dark Path?
questions.explanation_correct: Tolberti gives the player quests on the Dark Path in Might and Magic VII; Robert the Wise is associated with the opposing path.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Archibald is another character in the Dark storyline; Nighon is a location, not a path advisor.

questions.question: Which hero class has its own town type in Heroes of Might and Magic II?
questions.explanation_correct: Heroes II has distinct Wizard, Warlock, Sorceress, Knight, Barbarian and Necromancer town types.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Necropolis, Rampart and Tower are names of towns in Heroes III rather than Heroes II town types.

questions.question: What are blasters in the science-fantasy setting of Might and Magic?
options: A town type in Heroes II
questions.explanation_correct: Blasters are advanced energy weapons appearing in the series, not the name of an enemy species.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe different types of entities or locations.

questions.question: Which Heroes III Rampart Ranger has a Gold specialty?
questions.explanation_correct: Jenova is a Rampart Ranger whose specialty adds gold. Mephala is also a Rampart Ranger, but specializes in Armorer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dessa and Aislinn have different alignments; Mephala is a Ranger but not the Ranger with the gold specialty.

questions.question: What is the name of the elven forest kingdom in the Might and Magic series?
questions.explanation_correct: AvLee is the traditional elven kingdom in the Might and Magic lore. Harmondale is the land dispute site in MM7.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Erathia is the human kingdom, Bracada is the wizard land, and Harmondale is a specific border town.

questions.question: Which Heroes IV campaign follows the pirate Tawni Balfour?
questions.explanation_correct: Tawni Balfour is the protagonist of the Chaos-aligned campaign A Pirate’s Daughter.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other titles are campaigns associated with different heroes.

questions.question: What is the name of the cult encountered in Might and Magic VI?
questions.explanation_correct: The Temple of Baa is the cult encountered during Might and Magic VI.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are not the cult name requested.

questions.question: In Heroes III, what is the upgraded form of the Angel creature?
questions.explanation_correct: The Angel upgrades to Archangel in Heroes III. This is the more powerful version of the creature line.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are not the standard upgraded Angel in Heroes III. Only Archangel fits the creature upgrade.

questions.question: Which class is the Might and Magic VIII recruit Rohani Oscleton?
questions.explanation_correct: Rohani Oscleton is a recruitable Dark Elf; Devlin Arcanus is one of the available Necromancers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different character classes in the game.

questions.question: Which group contains only resources available in Heroes of Might and Magic II?
questions.explanation_correct: Mercury, sulfur, crystal and gems are all resources in Heroes II, alongside wood, ore and gold.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other groups do not list the Heroes II resource set.

questions.question: In Might and Magic VII, which potential successor to Judge Grey is associated with the Dark Path?
questions.explanation_correct: Selecting Judge Sleen leads toward the Dark Path; Judge Fairweather is associated with the Light Path.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lord Markham and Roland are different characters; Fairweather represents the opposing choice.

questions.question: Which Heroes III town can build a Skeleton Transformer?
questions.explanation_correct: The Skeleton Transformer is a Necropolis building that converts eligible creatures into skeletons.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other town types have different unique buildings.

questions.question: In Heroes III, which creature upgrades to an Evil Eye?
questions.explanation_correct: The Dungeon creature Beholder upgrades to an Evil Eye.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Medusas, troglodytes and harpies have other upgrades.

questions.question: Which flying Heroes III Tower creature upgrades from a Stone Gargoyle?
questions.explanation_correct: Stone Gargoyles upgrade to Obsidian Gargoyles in the Tower lineup.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other upgrades correspond to different Tower creatures.

questions.question: In the third Heroes installment, which faction features Knights, Angels, and Griffins?
questions.explanation_correct: The Castle faction is the standard human-themed army in Heroes of Might and Magic III.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rampart is home to Elves and Dragons, while Tower features Mages and Titans.

questions.question: Which two hero classes are associated with the Necropolis town in Heroes III?
questions.explanation_correct: Necropolis is the home town for Death Knights and Necromancers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other hero-class pairs are associated with different Heroes III towns.

questions.question: What is the starting town in Might and Magic III?
questions.explanation_correct: Fountain Head is the starting town in Might and Magic III. It serves as the player’s initial hub in the game.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are towns from other points in the series or the same game, but they are not the starting town in Might and Magic III.

questions.question: In Might and Magic III, whose journal accompanies the player’s journey through the Isles of Terra?
questions.explanation_correct: The Might and Magic III manual contains the journal of Corak the Mysterious.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are not the author of that journal.

questions.question: Who is Corak’s nemesis in Might and Magic III: Isles of Terra?
questions.explanation_correct: Corak’s journal describes Sheltem as his nemesis and warns of Sheltem’s plans for the Isles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other characters are not the nemesis named in Corak’s journal.

questions.question: Which Inferno unit is the upgraded form of the Devil in Heroes III?
questions.explanation_correct: A Devil upgrades to an Arch Devil in the Inferno lineup.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pit Lords and Efreet Sultans are also upgraded Inferno units, but they upgrade different creatures.

questions.question: Which flying Rampart unit upgrades to a Silver Pegasus in Heroes III?
questions.explanation_correct: The Pegasus upgrades to a Silver Pegasus in the Heroes III Rampart lineup.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Grand Elf is a different Rampart upgrade; the other options do not upgrade to Silver Pegasus.

questions.question: Which hero class belongs to Necropolis in Heroes III?
questions.explanation_correct: Death Knight is a Necropolis hero class in Heroes III. It is tied to that town’s undead theme.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other classes belong to different towns or alignments, not Necropolis.

questions.question: Which Heroes II town type is distinct from both the Wizard and Warlock towns?
questions.explanation_correct: Sorceress is a separate town type in Heroes II, alongside Wizard and Warlock.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Necropolis, Rampart and Inferno are town names used in Heroes III.

questions.question: What is the name of the advanced civilization associated with the Heavenly Forge in Might and Magic lore?
questions.explanation_correct: The Heavenly Forge is associated with the advanced technology of the Ancients in the original continuity.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are different groups or a dynasty within the setting.

questions.question: Which recurring barbarian hero appears in both Might and Magic and Heroes of Might and Magic?
questions.explanation_correct: Crag Hack is a recurring barbarian in the franchise. Kilgor is another barbarian character and is therefore not offered as a competing answer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The remaining characters are associated with different roles and factions.

questions.question: Which Heroes III realm is associated with the elves?
questions.explanation_correct: AvLee is the elven realm in Antagarich; Erathia is a separate human kingdom.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bracada and Deyja are associated with wizards and necromancers respectively.

questions.question: In Might and Magic VI, which town does the player begin in?
questions.explanation_correct: New Sorpigal is the opening settlement where the game begins. It serves as the starting location in Might and Magic VI.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are towns or regions from elsewhere in the game or series. They are not the initial town.

questions.subcategory: Heroes of Might and Magic III
questions.question: Which Inferno creature in Heroes III upgrades from a Hell Hound?
questions.explanation_correct: Hell Hounds upgrade to Cerberi in the Inferno creature lineup.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pit Lords, Arch Devils and Efreet Sultans upgrade different Inferno creatures.

questions.question: Which Light Path promotion can follow the Wizard class in Might and Magic VII?
questions.explanation_correct: The Sorcerer can first become a Wizard, then an Archmage on the Light Path or a Lich on the Dark Path.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lich is the Dark Path counterpart; Paladin and Ranger are different class paths.

questions.subcategory: Heroes of Might and Magic II
questions.question: Which two brothers contest the succession in Heroes of Might and Magic II?
questions.explanation_correct: Heroes II: The Succession Wars follows the conflict between Roland and Archibald Ironfist.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other pairs are not the two brothers in the central succession conflict.

questions.question: Which of these recruitable Might and Magic VIII companions is a Necromancer?
questions.explanation_correct: Devlin Arcanus is a recruitable Necromancer; Rohani and Cauri are Dark Elves and Fredrick is a Cleric.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other companions have different classes.

questions.subcategory: Heroes of Might and Magic III
questions.question: Which unit belongs to the Rampart faction in Heroes of Might and Magic III?
questions.explanation_correct: Centaur is a Rampart unit in Heroes of Might and Magic III. It is part of that faction's early creature lineup.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other creatures belong to other factions such as Inferno, Stronghold, or Dungeon. They are not Rampart units.

questions.question: Which alien invader leads the Kreegan threat in Might and Magic VI?
